title: trace-slab-simulator-epochal-regression-log
content:
Purpose and scope:

This doc captures a proposed lightweight simulator (trace-slab simulator) and an associated regression log/checklist we used while debugging recent perf regressions. The goal: translate production traces into an "epochal" slab schedule the scheduler/kernel-selector sees, run microbench-style probes against that simulated environment, fuzz KV cache eviction and prefix-caching behavior, and produce a reproducible perf run for CI/regression triage.

High-level idea (one-liner):
Turn request traces into time-ordered slabs (buckets of concurrent tokens + KV states) that are replayed across epochs. Each epoch feeds the kernel scheduler and KV cache with synthetic but realistic request interleaving so we can observe scheduler decisions and kernel fingerprint shifts without needing a full cluster replay.

Why this is different from existing harnesses:
- We operate at the slab/epoch abstraction so we can compactly model long-running KV churn (minutes -> epochs) while preserving microsecond-level scheduling choices inside an epoch.
- Built-in eviction-fuzz: intentional randomization of KV TTLs and churn patterns to surface eviction-related tail latencies.
- Exportable artifacts for kernel-selection telemetry: per-epoch kernel fingerprints and decision diffs that can be checked into regression rollouts.

Design components:
1) Trace ingestion and chunking:
- Input: compressed server trace (request start, latency, token_count, model_id, kv_accessed list, kv_hits, locality tag).
- Stage 1: normalize token counts to our internal token-slab size (default slab = 512 tokens).
- Stage 2: group requests into epochs (N seconds per epoch, defaults: 5s, 30s, 2m to support multiple fidelity runs).
- Output: epoch files that contain slab events, inter-request gaps, and aggregated KV state deltas.

2) Slab simulator:
- For each epoch, fabricates a set of concurrent execution lanes equal to peak concurrency for the epoch.
- Replays per-lane request sequences preserving ordering and inter-request gaps.
- Emulates KV cache semantics (LRU-ish with configurable eviction jitter) and prefix cache (configurable hit/miss probabilities derived from trace).
- Emits per-token kernel selection events (e.g., attention kernel X chosen at step T for lane L).

3) Eviction fuzzing layer:
- Configured with: base eviction policy (LRU/ARC), jitter amplitude (0..0.5), TTL noise (mean/std), and forced purge windows (simulate memory pressure).
- On fuzz runs, the simulator applies jitter to access timestamps and triggers evictions according to simulated GPU memory pressure spikes.
- Collects tail latency histograms pre- and post-eviction spikes to quantify sensitivity.

4) Kernel selection comparator:
- For each epoch, record the chosen kernel metadata: kernel id, estimated flop density, sequence length bucket, and trig points for fallback.
- Provide a textual diff between baseline run and current run highlighting kernel-swaps and step ranges where a different kernel was selected.

5) Probe microbench integration:
- The simulator exposes a "probe API" so microbench kernels (small synthetic workloads) can be injected at chosen epoch offsets.
- Useful to confirm kernel hotpaths or to validate measured FLOP/time per-step numbers when traces show unexplained increases.

Quick usage notes (local dev commands):
- Generate epoch files from trace: ./tools/trace_slab/ingest_trace --trace s3://traces/prod/2026-01-18.gz --epoch 30 --out /tmp/epochs
- Run simulator (baseline): ./tools/trace_slab/simulate --epochs /tmp/epochs --policy deterministic --out /tmp/simrun1 --profile
- Run with eviction fuzz: ./tools/trace_slab/simulate --epochs /tmp/epochs --policy lru --eviction-jitter 0.25 --pressure-windows "[60,120]" --profile --export-kernel-diffs
- Run microprobe injection: ./tools/trace_slab/simulate --epochs /tmp/epochs --probe /tools/microbench/fp16-attn --probe-offset 45 --profile

Observability outputs produced by a run (text/CSV/JSON):
- epoch_summary.csv: per-epoch concurrency, avg tokens, kv_miss_rate, peak_memory_sim
- kernel_fingerprint.json: ordered list of kernel choices per step (can be diffed against baseline)
- eviction_events.log: timestamps of simulated evictions and pre/post latency histograms
- simulator_trace_replay.txt: simplified textual timeline useful for humans

Regression checklist and triage guide (when you see a perf regression):
1) Reproduce on simulator with original production trace (start with 30s epoch). If no regression, try longer epochs (2m) to surface slow-growing KV churn issues.
2) Turn on eviction-fuzz with jitter=0.2, pressure-windows tuned to observed cluster memory loss events. Many regressions only show under fuzz.
3) Diff kernel_fingerprint.json vs baseline to see if a different kernel was chosen; if yes, correlate with token-length distribution changes in epoch_summary.csv.
4) Inject microprobe in suspect epoch offset to validate kernel perf numbers.
5) If kernel differences persist, run with disabled prefix cache to separate KV eviction effects from kernel selection differences.
6) If eviction spikes map to a particular model variant, pin that model in the deployment and re-run to confirm mitigation.

Recent mini-regressions observed (log excerpts):
- 2026-01-20: +18% p95 token-latency observed during daily spike. Simulator reproduction: reproduces with eviction-jitter=0.15 and pressure-window [100]. Kernel diff: swapped from kernel-a (fast matmul) -> kernel-b (safer path) at steps 320..390. Suspected: KV churn causing suboptimal kernel allocator fallback. Mitigation: reduced prefix cache TTL from 300s -> 120s and applied transient memory backpressure smoothing. Outcome: p95 back to baseline (+2%).
- 2026-01-31: intermittent p99 spikes on long-sequence evals. Simulator revealed prefetch miss pattern due to eviction window overlapping multi-request context. Patch: improved prefetch heuristic in kv-manager to bias toward multi-turn sessions. Follow-up: patched in PR 1482; still monitoring.
- 2026-02-07: increased step-level compute time for mid-length sequences. Simulator kernel_diff shows more frequent kernel-candidate filtering events; root cause traced to a recent kernel selector change that added an extra FLOP safety check. Rollback candidate created.

Open questions and TODOs:
- How to synthesize realistic cross-model routing in the slab simulator? (we currently coalesce by model_id but need better load-multiplexing heuristics).
- What is the right epoch durations matrix to run as part of CI? (fast CI: 5s/30s, nightly: 2m/10m?)
- Add a sanity-check layer that flags impossible kernel swaps (e.g., from 4-bit quantized to fp16) during simulation runs.

Attachments and artifacts to keep with run entries:
- link to original server trace (s3 path)
- kernel_fingerprint baseline commit hash (git sha)
- simulator config yaml used for run (eviction params, epoch length, probe offsets)

Notes to future selves:
- Keep simulator lightweight; we should avoid re-implementing the full runtime. Aim to emulate scheduling and KV semantics at a level sufficient to trigger the same kernel-selection and eviction behaviors we see in prod.
- When adding a new kernel selector heuristic, add a unit test that runs an epochal slab with churned KV to ensure no regression in kernel choice for existing fingerprinted traces.

Appendix: suggested short-term experimental plan (next 6 weeks):
1) Bake simulator into nightly regression suite, run two traces per model family (chatty multi-turn and single-turn long-seq) at epochs 30s and 2m.
2) Create a small corpus of synthetic churn patterns (steady, bursty, diurnal) to parameterize eviction-fuzz.
3) Add CI gate: if kernel_fingerprint diff > threshold (configurable) for a staged PR, fail fast and require engineer acknowledgment.

Contact and ownership: Aisha Desai (primary), Ravi Menon (kv-cache heuristics), Claire Huang (kernel-selector instrumentation).

End of doc.
